item.content:encoded: Several Planet 13 dispensary locations across Florida, including shops in Pace, Miramar Beach, Pensacola, Gulf Breeze, Panama City, and Tallahassee, closed early Saturday due to severe weather, according to a post on the company's Bluesky account. item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Regional Airport reported a wind gust of 50 knots (57.5 mph) from the north-northeast Friday evening around 10:40 p.m., according to automated weather station data. The airport also recorded heavy rain and mist, with visibility reduced to 2.5 miles. Lightning was observed in the distance to the south and southwest of the airport.

The conditions reflect what appears to be a strong weather system moving through the area. Residents and travelers should exercise caution during Friday night's weather, particularly those on area roadways where gusty winds and reduced visibility from rain could create hazardous driving conditions.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias Expected to Make Landfall This Evening; 72 mph Winds Already Battering Gulf Coast
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is moving toward landfall this evening along the Gulf Coast, with tropical storm-force winds already lashing the region, according to the National Hurricane Center. The NHC reported a 72 mph gust at Orange Beach, Alabama on Friday evening, giving a preview of what's expected as the storm makes its push ashore. Forecast models show…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is moving toward landfall this evening along the Gulf Coast, with tropical storm-force winds already lashing the region, according to the National Hurricane Center. The NHC reported a 72 mph gust at Orange Beach, Alabama on Friday evening, giving a preview of what's expected as the storm makes its push ashore.

Forecast models show the system will make landfall sometime tonight. Residents across the northern Gulf Coast—including the Pensacola area—should prepare for heavy rain, gusty winds, and potential storm surge. The storm's exact track and intensity at landfall will determine which communities face the most significant impacts.

Local officials urge residents to monitor updates from the National Hurricane Center and follow guidance from emergency management agencies. If you haven't secured loose outdoor items, charged devices, or prepared supplies, now is the time to do so. Check on neighbors, finalize evacuation plans if needed, and stay weather-aware through landfall.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Regional Airport recorded a wind gust of 50 knots (57.5 mph) from the north-northeast Friday evening, according to automated weather station data. The reading came in at 9:12 p.m. local time.

Conditions at the airport included rain and mist, with cloud cover at roughly 1,400 feet and visibility reduced to 4 statute miles. Barometric pressure measured 29.59 inches of mercury.

The gusts were part of broader weather activity moving through the region Friday evening.

item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service station at Naval Air Station Pensacola recorded a peak wind gust of 55 knots (roughly 63 mph) from the north-northeast Friday evening around 9:43 p.m., according to automated weather observations.

The reading came as light rain moved through the area, with cloud cover reported between 1,500 and 2,100 feet. Barometric pressure was falling at the time of the observation, with readings around 29.52 inches of mercury.

The strong gust was part of a broader wind event across the region, with sustained winds around 34 knots (39 mph) reported during the same period.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias 60 miles from Pensacola with 115 mph winds
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Pensacola area Friday evening, positioned about 60 miles south-southeast of the city and moving north at 17 mph with sustained winds of 115 mph, according to multiple weather reports. The northern Gulf Coast is already experiencing gusts approaching hurricane force. Orange Beach, Alabama has recorded wind…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Pensacola area Friday evening, positioned about 60 miles south-southeast of the city and moving north at 17 mph with sustained winds of 115 mph, according to multiple weather reports.

The northern Gulf Coast is already experiencing gusts approaching hurricane force. Orange Beach, Alabama has recorded wind gusts up to 72 mph, with similar conditions reported offshore near Pensacola at 69 mph, according to weather observers tracking the storm.

With the hurricane on a northerly track at that speed, the Pensacola area faces the likelihood of significant impacts in the coming hours. Residents and visitors are urged to secure property, seek shelter, and follow guidance from local emergency management and the National Weather Service.

The system moved through Escambia County with sustained tropical cyclone conditions. Residents in…
item.content:encoded:
A tropical cyclone brought gusty conditions to the Pensacola area Friday afternoon, with the National Escambia Mesonet station at NAS Pensacola recording a wind gust of 51 mph at 8:34 p.m. CDT, according to the IEMBOT Mob weather monitoring service.

The system moved through Escambia County with sustained tropical cyclone conditions. Residents in the area experienced the effects of the weather system through the evening hours.

No additional details about the storm's track, intensity, or expected impacts were immediately available. The National Weather Service in Mobile typically issues updated forecasts and warnings for tropical systems affecting Northwest Florida.

item.title: Post Offices Closed Monday for Columbus Day; Online Services Available
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service will close all post office locations across the region on Monday, October 12, in observance of Columbus Day. Regular mail delivery and retail services will resume Tuesday, October 13. While brick-and-mortar post offices will be shuttered, the USPS says customers won't be left without options. The postal service is directing…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service will close all post office locations across the region on Monday, October 12, in observance of Columbus Day. Regular mail delivery and retail services will resume Tuesday, October 13.

While brick-and-mortar post offices will be shuttered, the USPS says customers won't be left without options. The postal service is directing residents to usps.com, where they can order stamps and boxes, manage mail holds, process address changes, renew PO boxes, and print shipping labels online — all 24/7.

Many post office locations also feature self-service kiosks available around the clock, allowing customers to print postage for Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express shipments, purchase stamps, weigh and mail packages, and track deliveries. The USPS says it's expanding these kiosks and adding newer options like Rapid Dropoff Stations and USPS Smart Lockers at select locations as part of a broader modernization effort.

item.title: Tornado Watch issued for Okaloosa, Santa Rosa counties and Pensacola Bay area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a Tornado Watch for Okaloosa County, Santa Rosa County, and surrounding coastal waters including the Pensacola Bay area, effective as of Friday afternoon. The watch covers coastal waters from the Okaloosa-Walton County line to Pensacola, extending 20 nautical miles offshore, as well as Eastern…
item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a Tornado Watch for Okaloosa County, Santa Rosa County, and surrounding coastal waters including the Pensacola Bay area, effective as of Friday afternoon.

The watch covers coastal waters from the Okaloosa-Walton County line to Pensacola, extending 20 nautical miles offshore, as well as Eastern Choctawhatchee Bay and the immediate Pensacola Bay area. Residents and mariners in the affected zones should monitor weather conditions closely and be prepared to seek shelter if conditions worsen.

A Tornado Watch means atmospheric conditions are favorable for tornado development, though a tornado is not imminent. The National Weather Service recommends staying weather-aware, having multiple ways to receive alerts, and reviewing tornado safety procedures, especially for those in mobile homes or on the water.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias bears down on Pensacola with 120 mph winds, tropical storm conditions underway
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is closing in on the Pensacola area Friday afternoon, positioned about 145 miles south of the city with sustained winds of 120 mph and moving north-northeast at 16 mph, according to multiple weather reports. Tropical storm conditions are already beginning along the northern Gulf Coast, with the National Weather Service and local…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is closing in on the Pensacola area Friday afternoon, positioned about 145 miles south of the city with sustained winds of 120 mph and moving north-northeast at 16 mph, according to multiple weather reports. Tropical storm conditions are already beginning along the northern Gulf Coast, with the National Weather Service and local meteorologists urging residents to complete all final storm preparations immediately.

Life-threatening storm surge and devastating winds are expected as the hurricane approaches the region. Weather officials stress that the window for final preparations is rapidly closing, with conditions expected to deteriorate significantly over the next few hours. Residents in Escambia County, Santa Rosa County, and the broader Northwest Florida coast should ensure they have secured loose outdoor items, moved to their designated safe shelter, and stocked emergency supplies.

The forecast track has Isaias moving toward the north-northeast, which will bring the full force of the hurricane's core closer to the Pensacola metro area. Residents should monitor updates from the National Weather Service, Escambia County Emergency Management, and local authorities for the latest track and intensity information as the storm makes its final approach.

item.title: ECUA: Planned Water Shutdown Limited to Pensacola Beach
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The utility issued the clarification through its public information office to ensure customers throughout the service area understood the scope of…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority has clarified that a planned water and sewer shutdown announced Friday will affect Pensacola Beach only, not the mainland portion of Escambia County or Perdido Key.

The utility issued the clarification through its public information office to ensure customers throughout the service area understood the scope of the planned work. ECUA said the shutdown is limited in geographic reach, though the authority stopped short of providing specific details about timing or the reason for the maintenance.

While the planned shutdown won't affect most of the county, ECUA warned that storm-related water and sewer outages could still occur across its entire service territory, depending on weather conditions. The utility urged all customers to monitor official ECUA communications for updates on their water and sewer services.

item.title: Pace Water System issues precautionary boil water notice for all customers
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pace Water System has issued a precautionary boil water notice affecting all customers in Santa Rosa County, effective immediately as of Friday morning. The notice was prompted by the potential for water main breaks and other disruptions to the system. Until the water system has been fully evaluated and bacteriological testing confirms the water…
item.content:encoded:
Pace Water System has issued a precautionary boil water notice affecting all customers in Santa Rosa County, effective immediately as of Friday morning. The notice was prompted by the potential for water main breaks and other disruptions to the system.

Until the water system has been fully evaluated and bacteriological testing confirms the water is safe, customers should boil all water intended for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth, and washing dishes. Water should be brought to a rolling boil for at least one minute before use. Bottled water is also an acceptable alternative during the notice period.

The precautionary notice will remain in effect until Pace Water System completes a full evaluation and a bacteriological survey shows the water meets safety standards. Customers with questions or concerns can contact Pace Water System at 850-994-5129. Those wanting updates can also sign up for alerts through the utility's website at pacewater.org/subscribe.

item.content:encoded:
Multiple roadways and bridges throughout the Pensacola area and broader News 5 region are closing or have already shut down as Hurricane Isaias moves into Northwest Florida, according to WKRG News 5.

Authorities are urging residents to avoid travel on affected routes as the storm approaches. Specific road and bridge closures are being announced as conditions deteriorate throughout the day.

Residents should monitor local emergency management updates and news outlets for the most current list of closed routes and any additional precautions as Hurricane Isaias continues to impact the area.
